[The Basics of Working on Teams](https://hr.mit.edu/learning-topics/teams/articles/basics)

Summary

Not every work group is necessarily a "team"

Teams:
- Are collective as opposed to individualistic "work groups"
- Have a clearly defined purpose
- Have a shared commitment to the process and outcomes

Effective teams specifically have all the above characteristics as well as:
- Clearly defined roles and responsibilities
- Ground rules
- "Effective group process" which includes open communication and accountability

When all these conditions are met, working on a team can be an "exciting and empowering experience" where the team members work as a coordinated group to produce something bigger than themselves.
